item.title: Local connectivity of Julia sets of Newton maps of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Newton maps of $\sin z$, $\cos z$, $\sinh z$, and $\cosh z$, each of which is transcendental meromorphic and has infinitely many unbounded immediate attracting basins. We first verify directly that, for the cosine Newton map $N_{\cos}(z) = z + \cot z$, the half-planes $\{\pm \operatorname{Im} z > M\}$ are repelling petals at infinity for every $M \ge 2$. These explicit petals allow us to apply the tame-basin criterion of Bara\'nski, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpi\'nska and obtain local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin of $N_{\cos}$. We also show that the Newton map of $Ae^{\lambda z} + Be^{-\lambda z}$, where $AB\lambda \neq 0$, is affinely conjugate to the sine Newton map $N_{\sin}(z) = z - \tan z$. The published local-connectivity theorem for $J(N_{\sin})$ therefore applies to this entire family, including the cosine and the two hyperbolic Newton maps. We describe the invariant lines and basin geometry of the four maps and illustrate the corresponding dynamical planes numerically.
item.dc:creator: Molla Basir Ahamed, Sayantan Chakraborty

item.title: Dynabase: A Database of Extreme Examples in Arithmetic Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.26727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Dynabase, a database cataloging extreme examples in arithmetic dynamics related to several major open conjectures: the Morton--Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture and the dynamical analogue of Lang's conjecture on canonical heights, as well as data on postcritically finite maps and maps with nontrivial automorphisms. This database collects the known examples of extreme behavior for these problems and tracks the current status of subproblems based on degree and field of definition.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Hutz

item.title: Thurston measure is stationary with exponential Teichm\"uller moment
item.description: arXiv:2611.26798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1967, Furstenberg proved that every lattice in a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center admits a probability measure whose stationary measure on the associated Furstenberg boundary belongs to the Lebesgue measure class. We prove an analogue of this theorem for the action of the mapping class group on Teichm\"uller space. Every regular probability measure in the Thurston measure class on the space of projective measured foliations is the stationary measure of a non-elementary random walk with a finite exponential moment in the Teichm\"uller metric.
item.dc:creator: Alex Eskin, Kasra Rafi

item.title: Real-analytic actions of lattices in $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ on compact $n$-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.27055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify real-analytic actions of arbitrary lattices in $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ on compact connected $n$-manifolds without boundary, $n\geq 3$, with no invariant-volume assumption. After finite-index restriction, the action has finite image, extends to a connected Lie group locally isomorphic to $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ with an equivariant finite cover when needed, or is obtained by analytic surgery with at least one torus piece. In the last case the lattice is commensurable with a conjugate of $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb Z)$. As a main input, we prove a general cocycle superrigidity theorem for real analytic germs.
item.dc:creator: Federico Rodriguez Hertz, Zhiren Wang

item.title: Non-local ergodic measures in symplectic dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.27429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the direct product of two symplectomorphisms, one of which exhibits a basic set and the other one acts on a compact surface and has a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium. Under a local domination condition we show that a typical real-analytic perturbation of this system displays a large normally hyperbolic lamination on which the natural invariant measure is ergodic. The proof, which introduces a novel geometric source of semi-local ergodicity, combines tools ranging from KAM theory to geometric measure theory and is robust enough to be of interest in more general configurations.
item.dc:creator: Jaime Paradela

item.title: Rigidity and nonrigidity for interval translation maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.27528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Almost every infinite-type interval translation map in the Bruin--Troubetzkoy family, and in Bruin's family with any fixed number of branches, is rigid for its invariant probability, where typicality is understood with respect to the intrinsic induction parameter measure. We prove this by exhibiting explicit repeated-word blocks in the induction and showing that their cylinders recur. In the opposite direction, we give a sufficient condition for nonrigidity of a primitive aperiodic substitution: the existence of a rational periodic vector of its incidence matrix in the return-word space whose coordinate sum is nonzero. The proof gives a uniform positive lower bound for symbol discrepancies at all sufficiently large times. For self-similar Bruin maps with primitive period substitution, the same condition also implies weak mixing. We apply the nonrigidity condition to an explicit self-similar infinite-type Bruin map on eight intervals, specifying its algebraic parameters and verifying its return words.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Hubert, Alexandra Skripchenko

item.title: Real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices preserving an ergodic volume
item.description: arXiv:2611.27557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices that preserve an ergodic smooth volume on a compact manifold. On an invariant open dense set of full volume, the action is analytically conjugate to the restriction of an affine action on finitely many copies of one double quotient. The conjugacy carries Haar probability to the given volume. Analytic germ superrigidity supplies local coordinates with measurable dependence on the center. The conditional measures on coarse Lyapunov manifolds determine the law of a displaced center. A two-point joining pairs charts whose evaluations agree there and gives the change of coordinates. The resulting analytic frame bundle carries a coframe whose vector fields integrate to the homogeneous model. This gives the open homogeneous classification in Zimmer's program.
item.dc:creator: Federico Rodriguez Hertz, Zhiren Wang

item.title: Random pullback attractors for evolution equations with nonlocal perturbations and fractional Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.27687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study semilinear evolution equations with time-nonlocal perturbations of \(\mu\ge0\) and additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter \(H\in(1/2,1)\). Under the regularity assumptions and a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, we establish global existence and uniqueness in the concept of pathwise mild solutions. We overcome the difficult in which the solution family lacks the cocycle property, by shifting the corresponding stochastic Volterra equation on a weighted space, and then the continuous random dynamical system follows. Based on a dissipativity condition, we establish the pullback random asymptotic compactness and the compact random pullback attractor \(\mathcal A_\mu\). Finally, we prove that the family of random pullback attractors \(\mathcal A_\mu\) is upper semicontinuous at \(\mu=0\) almost surely.
item.dc:creator: Shiqi Li, Jiawei He, Jianhua Huang

item.title: Boundary of the Lagrange and Markov spectra near Hall's ray
item.description: arXiv:2611.27731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Lagrange and Markov spectra, denoted by $L$ and $M$, respectively, are closed subsets of the real line with intricate fractal geometry related to Diophantine approximations. In 1975, Freiman proved that both spectra contain the ray $[c_F,\infty)$, where $c_F=4.527829566\dots$, and that this ray is optimal, as both spectra avoid a tiny interval $(\nu_F,c_F)$. Using renormalization techniques and the thickness of Cantor sets, we prove that the boundaries $\partial L$ and $\partial M$ have positive Hausdorff dimensions arbitrarily close to $\nu_F$. Furthermore, in connection with Berstein's conjecture, which predicts that $[4.1,4.52]\subset L$, we exhibit a gap in $L$ near $4.08$, the first known gap in the region $L\cap[3.945,4.52]$. We also prove that the boundaries of both spectra have positive Hausdorff dimension near $4.5213$ and $4.08$.
item.dc:creator: Harold Erazo, Carlos Matheus, Carlos Gustavo Moreira

item.title: Recurrent sets and Lyapunov functions: from topological dynamics to weak KAM theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.27887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this survey is to clarify the intimate relations between Lyapunov functions and chain recurrent sets. The study of this subject comes from a seminal paper by Conley and has had recent advances by the so-called Weak KAM Theory for homeomorphisms. We provide a survey of the state of the art, presenting recent improvements and connections with the stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, in order to illustrate the distinctions between recurrent sets in a non-trivial case as well as their dependence on a parameter, we discuss a compartmental model from mathematical epidemiology and a fast-slow version of a prey-predator model with Allee effect.
item.dc:creator: Olga Bernardi, Mattia Sensi, Jim Wiseman

item.title: The Thurston algorithm for general entire maps on the complex plane: Existence and uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2611.27925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a marked topological entire Thurston map $(f,A)$ of stable parabolic type is Thurston equivalent relative to $A$ to a postsingularly finite entire function if and only if it has no Levy cycle relative to $A\cup\{\infty\}$. Here $A$ is a finite forward-invariant set containing the postsingular set. In the realizable case, the entire function is unique up to complex affine conjugacy, and every orbit of the Thurston pullback converges to its fixed point. We establish a Wolff--Denjoy type estimate for nonexpanding self-maps $T$ of the Teichm\"uller space of any connected orientable surface of finite type without boundary. If $T$ has an unbounded orbit, there are a nonzero measured foliation $G$ and a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{T^k x}(G)\le C\operatorname{Ext}_x(G)$ for every $x$ and $k\ge0$. For a fixed-point-free transcendental Thurston pullback, this supplies the foliation used in the existence proof. A central tool is a fixed finite measure obtained as the total-variation limit of renormalized pushforward measures transported back along a Teichm\"uller ray. It allows us to select a cylinder at a late time and compare the mass of the same marked region at different times. If $G$ has a cylinder, a four-point extremal-length estimate and the Thurston matrix force a Levy cycle. Otherwise, in the absence of a Levy cycle, cluster rescaling shows that cylinders of large modulus carry almost all the fixed measure at all late times. Following a cylinder of definite mass until its modulus decreases gives a contradiction. We compare this geometric argument with the proofs for real entire maps and exponential maps.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian van Strien

item.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.26707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $\sigma$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\in\sigma+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ the answer to the bi-Lipschitz question depends on the shape of the window rather than on the Diophantine properties of the plane.
item.dc:creator: Alan Haynes

item.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.
item.dc:creator: Jinbing Chen, Colin Grant, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky

item.title: Idempotent generically stable measures in NIP groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.27098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a global generically stable Keisler measure on a type-definable group in an NIP theory. Then $\mu$ is idempotent if and only if it is the unique translation-invariant measure on its type-definable stabilizer subgroup. This resolves the NIP case of the Idempotent Measure problem studied by Chernikov, Gannon, and Krupi\'nski.
item.dc:creator: Artem Chernikov

item.title: Convex Structure-Preserving EDMD: Passive Koopman Matrices as $Q$-Contractions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27730v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) approximates the Koopman operator using a matrix based on a finite set of observables. However, the least-squares matrix of a port-Hamiltonian (pH) system is generally neither passive nor invariant-preserving. We demonstrate that the implicit midpoint discretization of a lifted pH model precisely preserves energy balance, passivity, and all linear Casimirs for every step size. For a fixed storage metric $Q$, the resulting Koopman matrices are the Cayley transforms of $(J-R)Q$, where $J$ is skew-symmetric and $R$ is positive semidefinite. This set does not depend on the step size and is the closure of all Q-contractions. This set is LMI-representable; therefore, structure-preserving EDMD, including ports through a discrete-time Kalman-Yakubovich-Popov condition and Casimirs through affine constraints, is a semidefinite program. The constrained estimate is a projection of the unconstrained estimate in the data-weighted norm and cannot increase estimation error when the population target is pH-compatible. For every $Q$-contraction, a certified bound on the lifted prediction error grows linearly at most in time, whereas it grows geometrically for unconstrained models with Q-gain above one. Benchmarks on a damped pendulum and a damped rigid body demonstrate that constrained models never generate energy and that imposed Casimirs are maintained with solver accuracy (approximately $10^{-8}$). In contrast, EDMD may diverge or lose the Casimir with noisy data. The benchmarks also demonstrate that when $Q$ is the physical energy, the constrained models are less accurate than EDMD and can exhibit significant structural bias.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Ehrhardt, Achraf Zinihi

item.title: An arithmetic theory of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.27825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show geometric and dimensional properties of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra for both $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$ using the projective cocycle steering method, which we introduce. In particular, we show the existence of a simultaneous Hall ray for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, a simultaneous Hall interval for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$, regimes of full and positive Hausdorff dimension, a scaling law, empty low spectra in certain cases, a compact set of full Hausdorff dimension in $(2Q\sqrt 3 - \varepsilon, 2Q\sqrt 3)$ where $Q$ is a common denominator of the finite set of rationals giving the translations, and the density of Lagrange equality sets in $\mathbb{R}$ for Lagrange constants in the Hall ray or Hall interval, respectively. Furthermore, we show that the Lagrange equality set for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, for a finite set of rational translations, is thick but, for the set of all rational translations, is empty. Likewise, we bound the Hausdorff dimension of the Lagrange equality sets for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$ in every nonempty open interval of $\mathbb{R}$. For each fixed $Q$, our result on the Hall interval, the density result, and the dimension bounds for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(\delta)}$ hold for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$. Both emptiness results (low spectra and the Lagrange equality set under all rational translations) hold for every $\delta>0$.
item.dc:creator: Jimmy Tseng

item.title: An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line
item.description: arXiv:2512.23079v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $\alpha$-Kakutani substitution rule splits the unit interval into two subintervals of lengths alpha and $1 - \alpha$, for a fixed $\alpha \in (0,1)$. A simple inflation-substitution procedure produces tilings of the real line and their associated Delone sets. We show that there are precisely five distinct values of $\min(\alpha, 1 - \alpha)$ for which these sets are uniformly spread, meaning that they are a bounded displacement of a lattice. The proof of this surprising fact combines the construction and analysis of a related family of primitive substitution tilings, Solomon's criterion for uniform spreadness, and a classification of Pisot-Vijayaraghavan polynomials.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Yotam Smilansky. An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line. Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems 61 (2027), p. 105565
item.dc:creator: Yotam Smilansky

item.title: The regionally proximal relation for commutative semigroup actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.10397v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The regionally proximal and equicontinuous structure relations are fundamental relations in topological dynamics that capture the equicontinuous behavior in a topological dynamical system and its factors. For minimal actions of abelian groups, these relations are known to be equivalence relations that coincide. In this paper, we generalize these facts to semigroup actions: for minimal actions of commutative semigroups, the regionally proximal and equicontinuous structure relations are equivalence relations and the two coincide. We leverage our approach to prove a refinement: the regionally proximal relation for such actions is equal to an analogue and strengthening of Veech's D relation. We also develop the machinery of natural extensions for commutative, not-necessarily-cancellative semigroup actions that act by surjections, concluding that the maximal equicontinuous factor of a minimal action of a commutative semigroup is the same as the maximal equicontinuous factor of its natural extension. We formally verify all of the results in this paper in Lean. The main results are registered on Palomar, and we link to a Github repository containing code for the complete verification.
item.dc:creator: Angelina Blahodatna, Lauren Detmold, Daniel Glasscock, Anh N. Le

item.title: Quadratic Hubbard trees, automata, and ray connections
item.description: arXiv:2611.04190v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of angles whose dynamical rays land on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. We do this by extracting orbit portraits from angled internal addresses, and constructing a suitable Markov partition of angle intervals. A main application is computing direct ray connections between Hubbard trees in matings of quadratic polynomials, and understanding when ray connections between the trees first appear when moving along veins of the Mandelbrot set. If one of the mating parameters is fixed, we prove that first ray connections are picked up at parabolic parameters or tips of veins. We also prove that the locus of parameter pairs in two given veins for which there are no ray connections between the trees is open. Additionally, we show that there are no ray connections between small Julia sets in matings of locally connected rabbit tunings.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Ventilari Sodr\'e

item.title: Small scale quantum ergodicity in cat maps
item.description: arXiv:2005.00648v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study small scale quantum ergodicity in quantum cat maps, with semiclassical parameter 1/N, and prove three groups of results. First, for every N and every eigenbasis, almost all eigenstates are equidistributed on phase space balls of radius (log N)^(-a) for a<1/2, and on position space balls for a<1. For a set of N of full density and for Hecke eigenbases, almost all eigenstates, and even all of them, are equidistributed at polynomial scales. Second, every invariant probability measure is the semiclassical measure of quasimodes of order 1/log N, one for each N, that are not equidistributed at any scale between 4N^(-1/8) and a prescribed scale tending to zero. Third, there are orthonormal bases of quasimodes of order 1/log N for every N, and eigenbases for N with short periods, in which a full density subset is equidistributed at every fixed scale, but not at the scales (log N)^(-a) for a>1/2 in phase space and a>1 in position space. Hence, the exponents 1/2 and 1 in the first group are sharp: even for a full density subset of eigenstates, quantum ergodicity at fixed scales does not extend beyond the critical logarithmic scales.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Han

item.title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fr\'echet sequence spaces over trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.10053v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fr\'echet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of K\"othe spaces $\lambda_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.
item.dc:creator: Mateus Azevedo, Fernando Costa Jr., Jo\~ao V. A. Pinto
